what: Independent check of the corrected write-up of Addendum 8 (2026-11-11), made on a copy of the tree at commit 25d3780: every number against the stored files, every claim against the registration and the verification; each finding re-tested by a second reviewer.

lenses.coverage:
I checked every named part of the README sentence by sentence, plus the PR excerpt, against results/confirm.json. I recomputed the numbers myself with three scripts in <work>/find-numbers: rc.py, rc2.py and rc3.py. rc3.py regenerates FRESH-4 with fresh4.make() (no arguments, 800 tasks) and uses fresh4.provenance. It also re-evaluates the step-budget program for R3 with the reference evaluator at 2,000 and 200,000 steps.

What was recomputed from the stored rows:
- The loop table: unsolved tasks, teacher shares, taught, trials, accepted, learning counts, held-out B.
- The trial tallies from per-run solved sets: 18 rejected (16 net losers, 1 neutral, 1 gaining three tasks); 8 accepted symbols with a lost task; 3 accepted while the count fell.
- The cycle-2 symbol definitions; the FRESH-4 description and provenance (all tasks and list tasks).
- Every cell of the evaluation table, sound and verified; the generation-0 single runs and their union (125/116, verified 135/124); the 8 tasks that end at the top budget on a rejected (5) or not-sound (3) match.
- The primary comparison with its exact p; all five endings; verified and whole-pool readings.
- The symbol-stage stratum, with my own parser of task names: 250/506, 68 of 75, 65 solved with that very symbol, 41 of 42, 22 of 29, 42 vs 51, 57 vs 58, 67 vs 66.
- Every 'Beside the class' bullet: 50/26 and 82/23; 129 tasks and 125 vs 116; 349 tasks nobody solves; 387; new vs old by stratum; union 206; old vs generation 0; equal budgets on all 800; kinds of failure; the 44 other-output tasks; the pool reading; the new-only symbol counts; the seconds (1,192 and 857); spent shares of 75–91%.
- The criteria under all three measures; R3 by output type and against single runs (p 0.12 and 0.22); R1 gains and losses with p = 0.20.
- The R2 tasks and their symbols: 13 through s23_1 and 1 through s22_1 + s5_1; 11 programs with a (cons -1) sentinel; generation 0 solves none of them at any budget.
- The 13 and 4 discoveries and their kinds; the ablations (121, 61, 77); held-out B for R1, R2 and R3.
- The dev table, from the deepen_dev*_eval.txt files; FRESH-3 append-k (1 and 2 of 31) from replication.json; the budget formulas (259,100, 336,550, 596,568).
- The D1–D14 rows and the count of 15 misses among 61 predictions.
- The verdict row and its paragraphs; Limits 2, 6, 7, 8, 10–14; the files section.

The verification paragraph and the seventh-review bullets were checked against verification_addendum8.json: 16 files, 3 reruns, 38 vs 12, 74 of 367, 138 vs 100, 21 and 14 pool failures, 1 of 20 seeds, 15 findings with 12 confirmed.

About 420 numbers compared; about 413 match. The mismatches are the five findings above: 231/236, Limits 7's 56 vs 51, the four looser places, the 1,200–5,000 range, and seven budgets. The PR excerpt agrees with the README everywhere except that it repeats the 231-of-236 error.

Not recomputed (taken from the stored files, which agree with each other):
- Exact dream reproduction (42 vs 45, 546 tasks).
- Wide-input and whole-pool verdicts.
- Pre-Addendum-8 numbers quoted in Limits 2.

findings.title: The count of recomputed comparison items is wrong: the reviewer matched 236 of 241, not 231 of 236
findings.where: README 'What the verification confirmed' (Addendum 8 section); README 'Reviews', bullet 'What held' of the seventh review; PR excerpt, last paragraph
findings.quote: Of 236 comparison items recomputed from the stored rows, 231 match; the five that differ all come from the dream test above. / ... 231 of 236 recomputed items match (the other five through the dream test) / That last one confirmed the registered code, the registered set, 231 of 236 recomputed items
findings.explanation: Misstates. The verification file says 236 items matched and 5 more did not, so 241 items were compared and 236 matched. The report subtracts the 5 mismatches from the matched count, which understates the agreement and gives the wrong total. The same wrong pair of numbers appears in three places (two in the README, one in the PR).
findings.evidence: In verification_addendum8.json, the recount lens's coverage says: "In stored mode 236 comparison items (most of them multi-number dicts) matched and 5 did not." So 241 items were compared and 236 matched. The README gives "Of 236 comparison items recomputed from the stored rows, 231 match" (line ~738) and "231 of 236 recomputed items match" (line ~989). The PR excerpt gives "231 of 236 recomputed items". All three subtract the 5 mismatches a second time.
findings.correction: "Of 241 comparison items recomputed from the stored rows, 236 match; the five that differ all come from the dream test above." In the Reviews bullet: "236 of 241 recomputed items match (the other five through the dream test)". In the PR excerpt: "236 of 241 recomputed items".

findings.title: Limits item 7 still uses the uncorrected ending-4 numbers and the wrong stratum name
findings.quote: For the deepening loop, 125 against 116 (p = 0.13) without the tasks that contain `reverse` or `append-k`, 56 against 51 where no dream composed the pair of routines, 4 against 4 where a routine was never solved alone.
findings.explanation: Contradicts another part of the same report. The Addendum 8 section corrects ending 4 to 546 tasks, 58 against 51 (14 against 7, p = 0.095), and the seventh-review bullet says 'ending 4 is 58 against 51 on 546 tasks, not 56 against 51 on 544'. Limits 7 still gives the stored 56 against 51, so it understates the new arm's lead in that stratum. It also calls the stratum 'where no dream composed the pair of routines'. The registered stratum is 'no dream computes the task or composes its pair'. The pair-only stratum is a different set: 220 tasks have a dreamt pair, so 536 do not.
findings.evidence: README line ~1103 (Limits 7) says "56 against 51 where no dream composed the pair of routines". addendum8_checks.txt line 31, with element types compared, gives 546 list tasks and 58 against 51 (14 against 7, p = 0.09462). README lines 585-589 and 982-983 give the corrected 58 against 51 on 546 tasks. The registered stratum (PREDICTIONS.md lines 720-722, D7 at line 836) is "where no dream computed the task or composed its pair of routines", not only the pair condition. The D7 row (line 804) also gives the stored 56 against 51, p = 0.18, without a qualifier, but that row scores the registered prediction on the stored value, so it can stand.
findings.correction: "For the deepening loop, 125 against 116 (p = 0.13) without the tasks that contain `reverse` or `append-k`, 58 against 51 (14 against 7, p = 0.095; 56 against 51 as the script computed it) where no dream computed the task or composed its pair of routines, 4 against 4 where a routine was never solved alone."

findings.title: The 'four places' where the script is looser than the text leave out two of the reviewer's items, and one of those did happen
findings.where: README 'What the verification confirmed'; README 'Reviews', seventh review, bullet 'Confirmed, did not fire'
findings.quote: Four places where the script is looser than the registered text did not fire: the digest is checked on its first 16 hex digits, the missing-run check covers the FRESH-4 rows only, p-values are rounded to five decimals before they are compared with 0.05, and D5 and D9 would have been marked "not scored" ...
findings.explanation: Understates. The verification has two findings here. One lists five loose places, (a) to (e); the other covers D5 and D9. That is six places, and the README names four. Left out: (c) 'the largest runs come first' was implemented as every held-out B rung before the FRESH-4 rungs, so gen0@r181775:heldB ran before gen0@top:fresh4. This deviation did take place, which contradicts 'did not fire'; the reviewer judged it harmless. Also left out: (e) 'old against generation 0 up to C2old' is computed on all 800 tasks, while the item next to it uses the 756 list tasks.
findings.evidence: The conformance finding in verification_addendum8.json lists five loose places, (a) to (e). The D5/D9 scorer point is a separate finding. The README names (a), (b), (d) and D5/D9, and leaves out two. One is (c): every held-out B rung ran before the FRESH-4 rungs, so gen0@r181775:heldB ran before gen0@top:fresh4. The verification calls this order deviation harmless, but it did happen. The other is (e): 'old against generation 0 up to C2old' is computed on all 800 tasks against 756 for the item next to it; both give p < 1e-11. The Reviews bullet says "four places ... (the section lists them)", so the reader sees an incomplete list. No stored value changes.
findings.correction: "Six places where the script is looser than the registered text changed no stored value: the digest is checked on its first 16 hex digits, the missing-run check covers the FRESH-4 rows only, p-values are rounded to five decimals before they are compared with 0.05, D5 and D9 would have been marked "not scored" on a stratum that is not testable, where the text says they fail, the held-out B rungs ran before the FRESH-4 rungs (harmless, since the largest held-out B row ran first), and 'old against generation 0 up to C2old' is computed on all 800 tasks rather than the 756 list tasks (p < 1e-11 either way)." In the Reviews bullet: "six places where the script is looser than the registered text; none changed a stored value (the section lists them)."

findings.title: The candidate range for the nine R1 losses is slightly wrong
findings.where: README Addendum 8, 'R1, R2 and what the loop did', bullet on the nine losses
findings.quote: The nine losses are tasks the first cycle's vocabulary solved within 1,200 to 5,000 candidates and the final one does not solve within 10^4
findings.explanation: Misstates. The stored candidates-to-solution of the cycle-1 row on the nine lost tasks run from 1,179 to 5,001. Both ends fall outside the stated range. The breakdown (six drop-k k=5, two keep-mod-k, one modulo-k) is correct.
findings.evidence: I recomputed the losses as cycle1@student:fresh4 sound minus new@student:fresh4 sound. That gives 9 tasks, with cycle-1 candidates to solution of 1179, 1307, 1317, 4065, 4073, 4115, 4116, 4127 and 5001. Both ends fall just outside "within 1,200 to 5,000". This is a rounding slip only.
findings.correction: "The nine losses are tasks the first cycle's vocabulary solved within 1,179 to 5,001 candidates and the final one does not solve within 10^4" (or "within about 1,200 to 5,000 candidates").

findings.title: Held-out B union is now over eight generation-0 budgets, not seven
findings.where: README 'Verdict against the four criteria', second paragraph under the table
findings.quote: On the 124 held-out tasks the replication's state has 44 sound solves and generation 0 has 38 over the four budgets of the registered union, 39 over the seven budgets it has been run at, up to 1.1 million candidates per task.
findings.explanation: Misstates, and is stale since Addendum 8. In confirm.json generation 0 has been run on held-out B at eight budgets: 10^4, 10^5, 181,775, 251,479, 413,254, 569,881, 596,568 (new in this run) and 1,126,452. The verification uses the union of 'the 8 held-out B rows'. The count of 39 is unchanged.
findings.evidence: confirm.json has eight gen0 held-out B rows: student 10,000, deploy 100,000, r181775, r251479, r413254, r569881, C1new 596,568 and top 1,126,452. The union of their sound sets is 39. The verification also speaks of 'the 8 held-out B rows'. The count of 39 is right but the number of budgets is not. The same stale "seven budgets" also appears in the Addendum 8 section (line ~421).
findings.correction: Verdict paragraph: "... 39 over the eight budgets it has been run at, up to 1.1 million candidates per task." Addendum 8 section: "over the eight budgets generation 0 has been run at it is 44 against 39 (9 against 4, p = 0.13)."

lenses.coverage:
I read Addendum 8 in full (mechanism, evaluation set, outcome measure, primary reading and endings, the four criteria, the licence and what it would not license, the predictions and scoring rules) and all 15 findings of verification_addendum8.json (12 confirmed, 3 already disclosed). I then went sentence by sentence through: the deepening-loop part of 'Answer'; the whole Addendum 8 section (development table, cycle table, symbols, FRESH-4 description, evaluation table, primary comparison, endings, the ending-4 correction, re-pairing, the symbol-stage stratum, the descriptive bullets, the criteria table, the R3 paragraph, R1/R2 bullets, 'What the verification confirmed', 'Reading', 'What this does not show'); the predictions paragraph and rows D1-D14; the last verdict row and the two paragraphs under it; the seventh-review paragraph; Limits items 2, 6, 7, 8 and 10-14; 'Files and how to run'; and pr_body_excerpt.md.

I checked the numbers against addendum8_tables.txt, addendum8_checks.txt and confirm.json, and with my own scripts in work/find-claims (c1-c6.py). c1 evaluates the R3 program and the 10^5 step-budget program with the reference interpreter on 3,000 in-range inputs each and redoes the registered-sample verdicts. c2 lists the 9 R1 losses with their candidate counts, finds the identical step-exhausting program in cycle1@student and new@deploy, and counts the predictions table (61 predictions, 15 misses, consistent). c3 recomputes the primary and R1 under a consistent step rule. c4 scores R3 against single gen0 runs under sound, verified and pool. c5 checks the 8 tasks generation 0 loses at 1,126,452 (5 rejected, 3 not sound).

About 95 numbers compared (evaluation table, primary, endings, strata, kinds, dreams, symbols, clusters, leave-one-out, criteria under three measures, seconds 1,192/857, spend shares 75-91%, the 1,179-5,001 range of the losses, prediction counts 4/14 and 15/61, the review counts 15/12/3 and 231/236). All matched the stored data except where the findings say otherwise.

The issues are about readings, not arithmetic: R3 is overturned by a post-hoc, selectively applied step rule on a correct program; the verdict table column is scored inconsistently (R3 at the cumulative budget holds); the post-hoc stratum is unmarked in the Answer and PR; Limits 7 is stale; a conformance deviation that did occur is omitted; and the summary does not say the registration was not put to the Owner.

I found no overstatement against the licence on new routines, outputs, the procedure, time cost or open-endedness: all of these are disclaimed. D13 and D14 are scored as registered misses, and the count of 15 is consistent with that.

findings.title: R3 'does not stand' is presented as fact, but it rests on a post-hoc rule choice applied to a correct program, and that correction is applied only to R3
findings.where: README 'Answer' (third bullet on the deepening loop); 'A deepening loop...' paragraph '**R3 does not stand.**'; 'Verdict against the four criteria' (last row, R3 cell, and the paragraph 'R3 does not survive the verification... one of the final vocabulary's 126 verdicts is wrong by the audit's own rule'); 'Predictions' paragraph ('with that verdict corrected both predictions hold'); PR excerpt bullet 3
findings.quote: R3 does not stand. Its margin is one task, and on one of the 126 tasks the audit's verdict is wrong by the audit's own rule. ... The script's "all four: True" is therefore not a finding of this study.
findings.explanation: Misstates the registered result in both directions. (1) The program computes the task's function exactly; the only thing wrong is that it needs more than the evaluator's 2,000 steps on a few in-range inputs. The registered measure is agreement on the fresh inputs of oracles.fresh_inputs (up to 200). On that registered sample the verdict is (True, 200). So the registered verdict is not 'wrong by the audit's own rule'. The correction comes from inputs outside the registered sample (20 reseeds, a stress set) and from treating step exhaustion as wrong, which the registration does not state. Verification finding 3 (recount lens) says this itself: 'The registration ... does not say that exceeding the step budget counts as disagreement'. (2) The report is inconsistent about the step rule. At 10^5 it calls a program with the same defect 'a correct program stored as not sound' and offers 'Counted as sound it gives 172'. At 10^4 it calls this program's sound verdict 'wrong'. Under the 'computes the function' reading the report uses at 10^5, R3 is 126 against 125 and holds. (3) Even under the rule the report chooses, the correction is selective. The identical program text on the identical task is stored sound in new@deploy:fresh4 (inside the primary 171) and in cycle1@student:fresh4 (inside R1's 121). The report corrects neither. Applied consistently, the primary is 170 against 116 (75 against 21) and R1 is 61, 120, 125. (4) The verdict paragraph 'At its own student budget of 10^4 it is level with it or behind, depending on the measure' leaves out the registered measure, under which it is ahead by one. The accurate reading: as registered, R3 passes by one task, which is not separated from chance (p = 0.5). That task's program is correct but exceeds the step budget on unsampled in-range inputs. Under a stricter post-hoc step rule R3 ties, it ties on verified counts and it reverses on the pool. The pass is fragile and not upheld as evidence, but the registered verdict is a pass.
findings.evidence: Registration (PREDICTIONS.md 666-668) defines sound as agreement 'on the fresh inputs of oracles.fresh_inputs (up to 200)'. README itself says those 200 inputs hold no failing input, so the stored, registered verdict is True. The two reviewers disagree on whether exhaustion counts as failure: recount says 'The registration ... does not say that exceeding the step budget counts as disagreement'; criteria says Sound._agrees counts it. The README takes both sides. At 10^5 it calls a step-exhausting program one that 'computes the task' and adds 'Counted as sound it gives 172 against 116'. At 10^4 it calls this program's sound verdict 'wrong by the audit's own rule'. In confirm.json the same program text, (map (lambda x1. if (is_empty (filter (lambda x2. is_prime (x2+4)) (range x1))) 0 5)) x0, is stored sound for fresh4::((identify-geq-k 2)(replace-all-k-with-n 1 5)) in new@deploy:fresh4, cycle1@student:fresh4 and new-without-recursive@student:fresh4 as well as new@student:fresh4. Every gen0 row has (if (gt x1 1) 5 0), which is sound. The README corrects only the R3 instance. Applied the same way everywhere, the primary is 170 against 116 (75 against 21) and R1 is 61, 120, 125. None of this changes a class. The registered pass is disclosed in D13 ('the script prints a pass by one task'), so a reader is not misled about the scoring. The fault is the inconsistent wording and the selective correction.
findings.correction: Replace the opening of the paragraph with: "R3 as registered passes by one task: 126 against 125 (54 against 53, p = 0.5). That task's program computes the right function but runs past the evaluator's 2,000 steps on in-range inputs that the registered 200-input sample does not contain. If running out of steps counts as a failure, as Sound._agrees treats it, R3 is 125 against 125 and fails. The same program is then not sound in new@deploy or in cycle 1 either (primary 170 against 116, 75 against 21; R1 61, 120, 125). On verified counts R3 ties (135 against 135), and on the whole pool it reverses (105 against 112). The registered pass is not upheld as evidence." In the verdict paragraph, replace 'one of the final vocabulary's 126 verdicts is wrong by the audit's own rule' with 'one of the 126 rests on a program that exceeds the step budget on unsampled in-range inputs'.

findings.title: Verdict table: the column defines R3 as 'beats generation 0 at the cumulative budget', but the deepening row is scored against the union; at the cumulative budget it is 'yes' under every measure
findings.where: 'Verdict against the four criteria', last row, R3 column; the two paragraphs under it; 'Answer' first paragraph ('No loop of this study meets the four criteria fixed in advance')
findings.quote: | R3: beats generation 0 at the cumulative budget (sound) | ... | no. The script counts 126 against 125 for generation 0 at any of five budgets; one of the 126 verdicts is wrong, and it is 135 against 135 verified and 105 against 112 on the whole pool
findings.explanation: Understatement and inconsistency. The column header, the earlier rows ('no (30 against 37 at 413,254)' and so on) and the original criteria at the top of PREDICTIONS.md ('generation-0 machinery run once at the loop's cumulative budget') all define R3 as one generation-0 run at the cumulative budget. Addendum 8 registered a stricter union ('the union is stricter'). The deepening row uses that union under a header that says otherwise. At the loop's whole budget (C2new, 336,550, which the README itself calls 'the original wording of R3'), R3 is met on every measure, including after the step-budget correction: sound 126 against 113 (125 against 113 corrected), verified 135 against 124, whole pool 105 against 99. Against C2old it is 126 against 102, p = 0.0125. The README gives '126 against 113 ... (336,550; the original wording of R3; p = 0.12)' but never says that this meets the criterion fixed in advance. The Answer's 'No loop of this study meets the four criteria fixed in advance' therefore holds for the deepening loop only under the stricter registered R3 (and under the post-hoc pool reading for R1), not under the criteria as first fixed.
findings.evidence: PREDICTIONS.md line 27 has the original R3: 'beats generation-0 machinery run once at the loop's cumulative budget'. Addendum 8 (794-796): 'The original wording asks for generation 0 run once at the cumulative budget; the union is stricter.' The README column header (line 863) keeps the original wording, but the deepening cell scores the union. addendum8_checks.txt line 5 gives 'C2new 126 against 113 (59 against 46, p = 0.1207)', and addendum8_tables.txt gives verified 113/124 at C2new. The README quotes '126 against 113 ... the original wording of R3; p = 0.12' but never says this meets the original R3, which asks only for 'beats' with no significance test. Even with the disputed verdict removed it is 125 against 113. So the Answer's 'No loop ... meets the four criteria fixed in advance' holds for the deepening loop only under the stricter registered union. The other parts of the finding hold too.
findings.correction: Deepening row, R3 cell: "Registered (union of five budgets): no. 126 against 125, which rests on one disputed verdict; 135 against 135 verified; 105 against 112 on the whole pool. Original wording (one run at the whole budget, 336,550): yes, not separated: 126 against 113 (59 against 46, p = 0.12), 125 against 113 with that verdict removed." In the Answer, write: "No loop meets the four criteria as registered for it (for the deepening loop, R3 against the union of five generation-0 budgets) in a way that survives checking."

findings.title: The post-hoc symbol-stage stratum is given in the Answer, the Reading and the PR as the reading of the result, without the post-hoc mark, and the registered endings are not mentioned there
findings.where: README 'Answer', bullet 'Where the lead is'; 'Reading' paragraph ('there is none elsewhere'); PR excerpt bullet 2
findings.quote: In 68 of the 75 tasks only the learned vocabulary solves, one of the two stages is itself a learned symbol ... On the 506 list tasks with no such stage it has 67 against 75. ... Nothing shows a gain beyond that.
findings.explanation: Overstatement by omission of status. The section says 'This stratum was found by the verification after the run, so it is post hoc'. addendum8_checks.py says the same: 'a stratum chosen after the data were read'. The verification marks its p-values as descriptive. The Answer, the 'Reading' paragraph ('It is a result about memorised routines: ... and there is none elsewhere') and the PR excerpt give the stratum and its numbers with no post-hoc mark. Meanwhile neither the Answer nor the PR names the registered endings: ending 1 'also outside the routines of the earlier symbols' (42 against 10, p = 5e-6), ending 3 'with reach beyond the budget' (72 against 15) and ending 5 'also where a stage is not one of its learning tasks' (29 against 10, p = 0.0017). A reader of the summary sees the post-hoc reading in place of the registered one. Also, 'none elsewhere' is a post-hoc absence claim; at an equal budget of 10^5 the stratum is 67 against 66 (9 against 8).
findings.evidence: The section says 'This stratum was found by the verification after the run, so it is post hoc'. addendum8_checks.txt calls it 'a stratum chosen after the data were read', and Limits 14 marks it '(post hoc)'. The Answer bullet 'Where the lead is', the PR bullet and the Reading ('there is none elsewhere') give 68 of 75 and 67 against 75 with no mark. The numbers are right, and the reading is cautious: it declines a breadth claim that the registered endings 1 and 5 would allow. So the harm is small, but it is a missing qualifier.
findings.correction: Answer and PR: 'Where the lead is (post hoc, found by the verification). In 68 of the 75 tasks ...; registered endings 1 and 5 are significant but are carried by these tasks.' Reading: '... the lead is in the tasks where one stage is itself a learned symbol, and in a stratum chosen after the run there is none elsewhere (67 against 75).'

findings.title: Limits item 7 uses the uncorrected ending-4 numbers and a narrower stratum definition
findings.quote: 56 against 51 where no dream composed the pair of routines
findings.explanation: Misstatement and inconsistency. The section and the Reviews paragraph give ending 4 with the dream test corrected as 58 against 51 on 546 tasks (14 against 7, p = 0.095), as the verification confirmed. Limits keeps the stored 56 against 51 and leaves out the correction. It also describes the stratum as 'no dream composed the pair'; the registered stratum is 'no dream computes the task or composes its pair'.
findings.evidence: The README section (line 588) and the Reviews bullet give the corrected ending 4: '58 against 51 (14 against 7, p = 0.095)' on 546 tasks. addendum8_checks.txt has the same numbers. Limits item 7 (line 1103) says '56 against 51 where no dream composed the pair of routines'. That is the stored figure with no correction, and the registered stratum is 'no dream computes the task or composes its pair of routines'.
findings.correction: '56 against 51 as stored, 58 against 51 on 546 tasks (14 against 7, p = 0.095) with the dream test corrected, where no dream computed the task or composed its pair of routines'.

findings.title: 'Four places where the script is looser ... did not fire' leaves out a deviation the verification found that did occur (run order)
findings.where: 'A deepening loop...', paragraph 'What the verification confirmed'; 'Reviews', seventh review bullet 'Confirmed, did not fire'
findings.quote: Four places where the script is looser than the registered text did not fire: the digest is checked on its first 16 hex digits, the missing-run check covers the FRESH-4 rows only, p-values are rounded to five decimals before they are compared with 0.05, and D5 and D9 would have been marked "not scored"
findings.explanation: Softening by omission. Conformance finding 'Small places where the code decides more loosely than the text' lists five items (a) to (e), and D5/D9 is a separate finding. Item (c) is a registration deviation that actually happened. The registration says 'The largest runs come first', but all held-out B rungs ran before the FRESH-4 rungs (gen0@r181775:heldB before gen0@top:fresh4). The verification judged it harmless, but it fired. Item (e), the scope of 'old vs generation 0 up to C2old' (800 tasks against 756), is also missing.
findings.evidence: Conformance finding item (c): 'The largest runs come first is implemented as all held-out B rungs, then the FRESH-4 rungs ... gen0@r181775:heldB therefore ran before gen0@top:fresh4'. The verifier judged it harmless. The registration (PREDICTIONS.md 603) says 'the largest runs come first'. The README sentence about four places is true as far as it goes, but it omits a deviation that actually happened. Item (e) is a scope point with no effect.
findings.correction: Add after the list: "One deviation did occur, and it is harmless: all held-out B rungs ran before the FRESH-4 rungs, where the registration says the largest runs come first."

findings.title: The Answer and the PR do not say that the registration was not put to the Owner
findings.quote: A registered run printed all four as met on 800 new tasks. / A deepening loop, registered by the author under the standing instruction to continue
findings.explanation: The section says 'This registration was the author's and was not put to the Owner before the run'. The Answer, where a reader takes the result, calls it a registered run and does not qualify it. The PR says 'registered by the author' but not that the Owner did not see the registration before the run. Since the Owner's instruction was to continue until the criteria are met, this matters for how much weight 'registered' carries.
findings.evidence: The PR bullet already says 'registered by the author under the standing instruction to continue'. The section (README 450-451) states plainly that the registration was not put to the Owner. The Answer calls it 'a registered run', which is accurate: it was registered before anything ran on FRESH-4. Repeating the provenance in the summary is a matter of style.
